knowledgeAnswers.rationale: WorkSafe Victoria recommends on-tool extraction connected to a dust collector, with a minimum recommendation of Dust Class M. A dust bag alone does not capture fine dust efficiently.
WorkSafe Victoria lists dry sweeping as an activity that generates airborne wood dust, and does not present it as acceptable.
A HEPA vacuum is the recommended method for clothing. Compressed air re-suspends dust and can cause serious harm on skin.
WorkSafe Victoria and SafeWork NSW both recommend damping down the surface before sweeping.
Local exhaust ventilation captures dust close to each source and is inspected regularly, including checks for leaks in ducts.

practicalCriteria: Candidate connects on-tool extraction to a dust collector and HEPA vacuum, and records the check before the first pass.
Candidate seals the work area and closes doors to adjoining rooms before sanding starts.
Candidate performs clean-up using damp methods and a HEPA vacuum, with no dry sweeping and no compressed air used at any stage.
Candidate bags and labels dust and waste according to the approved procedure, and records the controls used.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Dust control record for the room
stopWorkCriteria: Sanding started with extraction not connected or not working
Dry sweeping or compressed air used on the floor, a bench, skin or clothing
Occupants present in the sanding area
